seoTitle: Free CSS Scrollbar Generator with Live Preview
metaDescription: Free CSS scrollbar generator. Style scrollbars with ::-webkit-scrollbar and the standard scrollbar-color and scrollbar-width. Live preview included.
intro: Style scrollbars for any selector using both the standard scrollbar-color and scrollbar-width properties and the older ::-webkit-scrollbar rules. Choose colours, width and radius and see a live preview.
why:
The default scrollbar often clashes with a dark theme or a custom interface. Styling it has been messy for years, because browsers split into two approaches: the standard properties, now supported in current Firefox and Chromium, and the older ::-webkit-scrollbar pseudo-elements that Safari and some other browsers still depend on.

Pick the selector, thumb, hover and track colours, a width and a thumb radius, and the tool writes both sets of rules together so the result is consistent across browsers. A scrolling demo box shows how it looks. Remember that very thin or low-contrast scrollbars hurt usability, and that hiding them entirely with scrollbar-width: none removes a visual cue that content scrolls. Nothing is uploaded.
howTo: Enter the CSS selector, for example .scroll.
Choose the thumb, hover and track colours, the width and the thumb radius.
Pick the standard scrollbar-width: thin, auto or none.
Check the preview and copy the CSS.

faq.q: Why are there two sets of rules?
faq.a: scrollbar-color and scrollbar-width are the standard properties. The ::-webkit-scrollbar rules give finer control and are still needed for older Safari and Chromium versions, so both are included.

faq.q: Does the hover colour work everywhere?
faq.a: Hover styling applies through the WebKit rules only. Browsers that use the standard properties show the single thumb colour you set.

faq.q: Can I apply it to the whole page?
faq.a: Yes, use html or body as the selector. For the page scrollbar, some browsers apply styles from the root element only, so try html first.

faq.q: Is hiding the scrollbar a good idea?
faq.a: Use scrollbar-width: none with care. Users may no longer see that content scrolls, which hurts usability and accessibility. Keep a visible cue or keep the scrollbar thin.
